runs.title: Curiosity's dawn-on-Mars photo from NASA
runs.prompt: NASA's Curiosity rover has captured an image of dawn on Mars. Find the original NASA or JPL page about it: What does the image show, and when was it taken?
runs.answer: NASA's Curiosity rover captured a Mastcam panorama of dawn (sunrise) on Mars, showing striking blue hues in the foreground as bright morning light illuminates distant, wind-carved cliffs called "yardangs" on the northwestern shoulder of 3-mile-tall Mount Sharp (Gale Crater). The image is a stitching of six individual Mastcam frames processed without the usual white balancing, to preserve the early-morning look. It was taken at 8:30 a.m. local Mars time on Aug. 11, 2026 — the 4,982nd Martian day (sol) of the mission. The original NASA page is the news article "NASA's Curiosity Rover Catches Stunning Martian Dawn" (published Oct. 6, 2026), with the matching image entry PIA25629 in NASA's Photojournal; credit NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS.

runs.title: McDonald's AI pricing suit: what it claims
runs.prompt: McDonald's is being sued over an AI pricing tool used to recommend prices to U.S. franchisees. Find a non-paywalled news source and report: who filed the lawsuit, in what court, and what the suit claims McDonald's did.
runs.answer: Michael Thomas, a consumer from DeKalb, Illinois (a frequent McDonald's customer), filed a proposed nationwide class-action lawsuit. It was filed Friday, October 2, 2026, in federal court in Chicago, Illinois. The suit claims McDonald's violated U.S. antitrust law by running an AI-enhanced pricing tool that gathers nonpublic data competitors wouldn't normally share (like store-level sales) and shares it among franchisees who may compete in the same market — amounting to "algorithmic price-fixing." It also alleges McDonald's uses its leverage over franchisees to pressure them to follow its recommended prices and blames the tool for driving up U.S. menu prices; it seeks class certification, damages, and an injunction against competition-restricting agreements. McDonald's denies the claims, saying "AI does not set menu prices" and calling the suit "filled with inaccuracies."
